key_insight: Re-Search turns research ideation into a Twenty Questions–style game: an LLM receives a published paper's research problem and asks yes-or-no questions to rediscover its core idea. This makes the model's step-by-step exploration visible rather than judging only its final proposal.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations obscure how LLMs search through research ideas, making it difficult to identify where their reasoning progresses or stalls.
method: Give the model only the research problem from a published paper, withholding its core idea.
Have the model ask yes-or-no questions to progressively narrow down possible solutions.
Use the questioning process to examine how the model explores and refines ideas; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not report results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Re-Search offers a way to evaluate the process behind AI-generated research ideas, not just their final quality. It could help diagnose weaknesses in iterative ideation and guide better research assistants.
visual_elements: Two-player diagram showing an LLM questioner exchanging yes-or-no questions and answers with a responder.
Branching decision tree illustrating how answers narrow the space of possible research ideas.
Step-by-step timeline from research problem to questions, refinements, and a proposed core idea.
Side-by-side comparison of final-output evaluation versus process-visible evaluation.
paper_title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
paper_authors: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su, Yu Zhang, Daniel Khashabi
